https://pancanal.com/wp-content/uploads/.text: ADVISORIES ARE AVAILABLE AT http://www.pancanal.com FOR ETAS OR DIRECT COMMUNICATION WITH OUR OFFICES, REFER TO NOTICE N-3-2023 Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory To Shipping No. A-39-2026 October 21, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System Considering the effectiveness of the water saving measures implemented at the Locks and the positive impact of recent close to average precipitation levels on the Canal watershed, the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) has been able to sustain the number of transits being offered at the Panamax Locks, therefore, effective immediately, we are pleased to announce the reinstalment of the Last-Minute Reservation service at the Panamax Locks. The Last-Minute Reservation service will be made available in accordance with the criteria and rules set forth in Notice to Shipping N-07 when a slot becomes available and the ACP, at its sole discretion, decides to offer such slot. Additionally, the rules mentioned in the Notice to Shipping N-07, article 23, section 12, regarding the rules for Swaps and Substitutions between Alliance Members that were only available for Neopanamax vessels, will also be available for vessels in the Super category for booking dates beginning January 3, 2027. Please note that all other Swap and Substitution rules set forth in the N-07 remain in effect. While the water deficit in the Canal watershed persists, the Transit Reservation (Booking) System remains the only mechanism to guarantee a transit date. Therefore, vessels without a reservation may experience extremely extensive delays. The Canal remains committed to closely monitoring water conditions and rainfall levels and will communicate any further adjustments in a timely manner, as circumstances warrant. For inquiries regarding these measures, please contact: operationservices@pancanal.com ORIGINAL SIGNED Boris Moreno Vásquez Vice President for Operations 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023

https://pancanal.com/wp-content/uploads/.text: ADVISORIES ARE AVAILABLE AT http://www.pancanal.com FOR ETAS OR DIRECT COMMUNICATION WITH OUR OFFICES, REFER TO NOTICE N-3-2023 Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory To Shipping No. A-37-2026 October 5, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Long-Term Slot Allocation Program 2027 and Modification to Transit Reservation System tariffs To facilitate customer planning for the 2027 dry season, the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) will offer Long- Term Slot Allocation (LoTSA) programs for transit dates from January 3 through April 3, 2027. LoTSA Neopanamax will continue under its current terms, while the new LoTSA Panamax Pilot Program will extend advance slot allocation to customers transiting the Panamax Locks. What the program is designed to do LoTSA allows customers to secure a package of transit slots for the full period in a single transaction, reducing their reliance on daily booking competitions. By committing part of the Canal’s projected transit capacity earlier, the program enhances planning certainty, particularly when water availability is limited. Neopanamax: continuity for customers with recurring itineraries LoTSA Neopanamax will continue under the current award mechanism, selection criteria, and tie-breaking rules, with an average of three (3) slots per day. Customers may therefore secure transits for the full period under familiar terms. Panamax: a new planning option for segments that did not have one For the first time, customers transiting the Panamax locks may secure slots in advance through a sealed-bid auction. The pilot will use the same award mechanism, selection criteria, and tie-breaking rules as LoTSA Neopanamax and will offer an average of three (3) slots per day. It is intended for fixed-itinerary customers and those whose customer-ranking position makes it more difficult to obtain slots through the regular booking system. How are the slots offered? • Only Fixed packages will be offered, with a single level of flexibility and characteristics tailored to the operational needs of eligible segments. • Slots will be distributed according to package type and transit direction, for each set of locks. • A new FixSlot package is introduced for all other market segments, excluding Full Container, LNG, and LPG vessels. Key dates Event Neopanamax Panamax Competition November 17, 2026 10:00 A.M. to 12:30 P.M. November 24, 2026 (Sealed bids accepted from 10:00 A.M. to 2:30 PM) Implementation November 29, 2026 (First priority booking window) December 16, 2026 (First priority booking window) Booking dates Next cycle announcement January 3, 2027 to April 3, 2027 January 2027 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 OP, October 5, 2006 Subject: Long-Term Slot Allocation Program 2027 and Modification to Transit Reservation System tariffs Detailed terms and conditions will be available in the following link: https://pancanal.com/en/lotsa/ The three slots allocated to LoTSA in the Panamax Locks will be reduced during Period 1 and Period 2, as indicated below. Consequently, for booking dates beginning January 3, 2027, four (4) slots may become available upon the opening of the 1st Period Competition on October 5, 2026, and seven (7) slots may become available upon the opening of the 2nd Period Competition on December 20, 2026. The following tables summarize the slot distribution per Booking Period for the Neopanamax and Panamax Locks: For booking dates beginning January 3, 2027, to April 3, 2027 Modifications to Booking Late Cancellation Surcharge fee Effective October 15, 2026, the ACP will temporarily modify the Booking Late Cancellation Surcharge under tariff 1050.IBC9, previously announced in Advisory No. A-28-2026, by reducing the applicable cancellation threshold from seven (7) days to four (4) days. The surcharge will apply to cancellations received four (4) days or less before the required arrival time and to vessels that fail to arrive within seven days after that time. It remains at 250% of the reservation fee, in addition to charges under tariffs 1050.IBC4, 1050.IBC5, and 1050.IBC10, and will remain in effect until further notice. TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Clarification on Consecutive Booking Dates Limitation in the Panamax Locks Across Different Booking Periods The Panama Canal Authority hereby clarifies the application of the booking eligibility rules related to consecutive booking dates in the Transit Reservation System for the Panamax Locks. This clarification is provided in connection with the provisions introduced through Advisory to Shipping No. A-28-2026 regarding booking slot eligibility across competitions and special competitions conducted in different booking periods. All other Panamax booking slot allocation rules published in Advisory to Shipping No. A- 28-2026 remain in effect and are not affected by this clarification. Effective immediately, the restriction on obtaining booking slots for consecutive transit dates shall not apply when the bookings are awarded through different booking periods. This clarification applies exclusively to Panamax Locks. Accordingly, a customer that has been awarded a booking slot for a transit date during Booking Period 1 may also participate in, and be awarded, a booking slot for the following transit date during Booking Period 2, subject to slot availability and compliance with all other applicable reservation process requirements. This clarification is intended to ensure a consistent interpretation of the current rules, avoid unintended restrictions and provide customers with greater clarity and predictability when planning multiple transits. Consequently, the consecutive booking date limitation shall apply only within the same booking period and shall not prevent customers from obtaining booking slots for consecutive transit dates when such slots are awarded through different booking periods. For any further inquiries regarding these rules, please contact: operationservices@pancanal.com. ORIGINAL SIGNED Boris Moreno Vásquez Vice President for Operations 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023

The maximum sustainable capacity of the Panama Canal (Panamax and Neopanamax Locks) is approximately 36-38 vessels per day. * In order to perform scheduled maintenance works ** In order to perform scheduled dry chamber works *** Culvert outage 3654 (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 OP, September 10, 2026 Subject: Monthly Canal Operations Summary August 2026 Ilya Espino de Marotta Takes Office as Administrator of the Panama Canal Engineer Ilya Espino de Marotta took office as Administrator of the Panama Canal on Monday, September 7, 2026, for the 2026–2033 term. The ceremony formalized an orderly leadership transition and marked the beginning of a new administration leading the institution. With more than four decades of service, Espino de Marotta becomes the first woman to hold the Panama Canal’s highest executive position. “Forty-one years ago, I came here to learn. Today, it is my turn to lead, but my conviction remains exactly the same; to serve Panama with honesty, discipline, and profound respect for this institution,” Espino de Marotta said. “My commitment is to remain focused on efficiency, transparency, and ethics, because every dollar we manage at the Canal belongs to Panama, and that is how we will treat it,” she added. “I accept this appointment with a profound sense of duty and with absolute confidence in the people who make it possible to run the Canal every day.” Espino de Marotta assumes the role of Administrator following a career spanning the Canal’s technical, operational, and executive areas. She began her career in 1985 as a marine engineer and the only female engineer at the shipyard of what was originally the Industrial Division. She later worked in the Engineering Section of the Dredging Division, the Mechanical Engineering Section of the Engineering Division, and the Accounting Division, where she served as a valuation engineer. She also served as coordinator of the Maritime Operations Department’s Investment Program and was a member of the Canal Master Plan Coordination Team. She also worked in the Program Development Office and served as executi ve manager of Resource Administration and Project Controls. Later, she served as Executive Vice President for Engineering and Program Management where she played a key role in the execution and completion of the Panama Canal Expansion Program, which is one of the most significant engineering and management undertak ings in Panama’s history. Following the project’s completion, she served as Vice President for Operations and, in 2019, was appointed Deputy Administrator of the Panama Canal, assuming the position on January 1, 2020. In January 2024, she was appointed the Panama Canal’s first Chief Sustainability Officer. 3654 (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 OP, September 10, 2026 Subject: Monthly Canal Operations Summary August 2026 The ceremony was held at the Administration Building and was attended by the President of the Republic of Panama José Raúl Mulino; Minister for Canal Affairs and Chairman of the Board of Directors José Ramón Icaza ; members of the Board of Directors; outgoing Administrator Ricaurte Vásquez Morales; government officials, and other Canal employees. “With this inauguration, Panama demonstrates once again its ability to transfer the leadership of its most important asset through strong governance, clear rules and processes, and institutions that work,” Minister Icaza said. “All Panamanians should be proud of our Canal. Let us support the leadership of the new Administrator,” he added. Administrator Espino de Marotta will be responsible for implementing the Panama Canal’s 2025–2035 Strategic Vision. This roadmap seeks to ensure water security, strengthen the reliability and resilience of Canal operations, diversify its services , and consolidate Panama’s position as a global logistics, maritime, and energy hub. Priority initiatives include the development of the Río Indio reservoir, new port terminals on the Atlantic and Pacific coast s, an energy corridor, and a logistics corridor. These projects are intended to expand the Panama Canal’s capabilities and revenue sources, strengthen the competitiveness of the route, and increase its contribution to the country. The administrator holds a bachelor’s degree in Marine Engineering from Texas A&M University and a master’s degree in Economic Engineering from Universidad Santa María La Antigua. Her professional education also includes executive programs at INCAE Business School and Northwestern University’s Kellogg School of Management, as well as a project management certification from the Project Management Institute. The inauguration marks a new chapter in the history of the Panama Canal and reinforces the continuity of an institution built on merit, experience, and the orderly succession of its leadership. With this transition, the Canal enters a new stage focused on preserving its strategic role in global trade while expanding the benefits it generates for Panama.

These revisions will prevent misunderstandings and unintended interpretations that could affect the transparency, consistency, and overall effectiveness of the booking process. Therefore, effective immediately, the following changes will be implemented: The paragraph in the Article 22, section “6. Booking Period 1A for Neopanamax Vessels” on page 6 of Notice to Shipping N07: “Priority will also be given to full container vessels when assigning slots carried over from Period 1 and slots that are cancelled or become available due to other reasons” will be replaced by the following paragraph “Slots that are cancelled or become available due to any reason will be allocated through a Special Competition in the following priority order, based on customer ranking: LNG, LPG, Car Carrier/RoRo and Full Containers” The paragraph in the Article 22, section “12. Last Minute Transit Reservation” on page 11 of Notice to Shipping N07, regarding the requirements vessels must comply to be offered a Last Minute Transit Reservation: “Vessels that have tried to obtain a booking slot during any booking period and through an auction for a transit date; or” will be replaced by the following paragraph “Vessels that have tried to obtain a booking slot during any booking period by participating in a Tiebreaker or Special competition and through an auction for a transit date; or” In the Advisory ADV-28-2026, the following paragraph “Customers that have already been awarded booking slots in previous periods, including Long Term Slot Allocation (LoTSA) and Net Zero for the same booking date, will not be allowed to obtain a slot during current competition, unless there are no additional competitors” will be replaced by the following paragraph: “Customers that have already been awarded booking slots in previous periods, through competition, a first come first served slot allocation option that becomes available upon the conclusion of the competition, Long Term Slot Allocation (LoTSA) or Net Zero for the same booking date, will not be allowed to obtain a slot during current competition, unless there are no additional competitors.” Additionally, in the same Advisory, “Customers that have previously been awarded booking slots on the previous booking date, including LoTSA and Net Zero, will not be allowed to obtain a slot during the following booking date competition, unless there are no additional competitors”, will be replaced by the following paragraph: “Customers that have previously been awarded booking slots on any booking date through competition, a first come first served slot allocation option that becomes available upon the 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 OP, August 25, 2026 Subject: Modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System conclusion of the competition, LoTSA or Net Zero, will not be allowed to obtain a slot during the previous or following booking date competition, unless there are no additional competitors.” Furthermore, for a NetZero slot, Swaps are permitted only between vessels that meet the same eligibility criteria used for the original slot allocation, including the same PCUMS tonnage. In contrast, for a Substitution, the vessel receiving the slot may have a PCUMS tonnage equal to or greater than that of the vessel originally allocated the slot. For any further inquiries regarding these rules, please contact: operationservices@pancanal.com. ORIGINAL SIGNED Boris Moreno Vásquez Vice President for Operations

https://pancanal.com/wp-content/uploads/.text: ADVISORIES ARE AVAILABLE AT http://www.pancanal.com FOR ETAS OR DIRECT COMMUNICATION WITH OUR OFFICES, REFER TO NOTICE N-3-2023 Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory to Shipping No. A-29-2026 August 20, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Additional Measures to Address Reduced Precipitation in the Canal Watershed Despite the arrival of the rainy season in the Isthmus of Panama and the water-saving measures implemented by the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) in recent months to mitigate the adverse effects of the El Niño event, current watershed conditions continue to warrant additional preventive measures to support the long-term sustainability of Canal operations. During the current hydrological year (May through August), cumulative rainfall across the Canal watershed has been 34% below the historical average, while watershed inflows have been 44% below their historical average for the same period, reflecting a substantially reduced hydrologic response despite the onset of the rainy season. Furthermore, forecasts indicate that the anticipated severity of the 2026-2027 El Niño event could further reduce precipitation and runoff during the remainder of the wet season. The combination of these observed deficits and the forecast of a potentially severe 2026-2027 El Niño event raises concerns regarding water availability during the upcoming 2027 dry season (January to April). These conditions require vigilant monitoring and prudent water resource management to always ensure the reliable and sustainable operation of the Canal. Particularly during the 2023-2024 El Niño event, the Canal maintained full open and timely communications with agents, owners and operators on the existing hydrological conditions of the waterway, a practice that we maintain at all times regardless of its criticality, as these hydrological conditions, is an essential aspect of our mutual interest. The measures described below are therefore being implemented to preserve service reliability, safeguard water resources for human consumption, and provide customers with timely and transparent information to support voyage planning and supply chain decisions. Effective August 21, 2026, for booking dates beginning September 4, 2026, the number of daily slots available at the Neopanamax Locks will be adjusted to nine (9). Accordingly, only one (1) slot will be offered during Booking Period 2. Additionally, the number of daily slots available at the Panamax Locks will be adjusted to twenty-five (25). Accordingly, only one (1) slot will be offered to Regular vessels during Booking Period 2. Due to the reduction in available transit slots during Booking Period 2, Conditioned slot in the Neopanamax category will not be available. 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 OP, August 20, 2026 Subject: Additional Measures to Address Reduced Precipitation in the Canal Watershed 2 The following table summarizes daily slot availability by vessel category: Effective August 21, 2026, for booking dates beginning September 4, 2026 Moreover, effective September 1, 2026, for booking dates beginning September 15, 2026, the number of daily slots available at the Panamax Locks will be adjusted to twenty-three (23). Furthermore, the maximum authorized draft adjustment of 14.48 meters (47.5 feet) TFW, scheduled to become effective on September 3, 2026, will be postponed until October 1, 2026. https://pancanal.com/wp-content/uploads/.text: ADVISORIES ARE AVAILABLE AT http://www.pancanal.com FOR ETAS OR DIRECT COMMUNICATION WITH OUR OFFICES, REFER TO NOTICE N-3-2023 Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory to Shipping No. A-28-2026 August 20, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Transit Reservation (Booking) System - Rule modifications The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) continues to experience climatic disruptions due to the current El Niño event, which is causing below-average rainfall and reduced water inflows to its reservoirs. To help ensure reliable Canal operations and preserve the draft available to customers, the ACP is introducing temporary modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System. These changes are intended to allocate slots in the most equitable manner as possible, across market segments and prioritize vessels that make more efficient use of water. The following measures will take effect on the dates indicated below. Auctions methodology Given the current climate conditions and to promote a more equitable allocation process, considering market composition, including cargo type, market segment characteristics, and vessel operating models, the ACP will temporarily make selected auction slots available by market segment group. Similarly to what was temporarily implemented on November 29, 2023, this method aims to provide additional opportunities for different market segment vessels. Effective August 21, 2026, for booking dates beginning September 4, 2026, auction slots designated for Neopanamax, Super and Regular vessels may be made available to vessels within specific market segments, organized into groups, as shown in the following table: Group 1 Group 2 Group 3 Group 4 • Liquified Natural Gas • Liquified Petroleum Gas • Dry Bulk • General Cargo • Others • Full Container • Vehicle Carriers / RoRo • Refrigerated • Chemical Tankers • Crude/Product Tankers The ACP will announce the day of the week on which the auction slot will be made available to each group. The specific dates on which the groups (one or more) identified above may participate in the auctions will be determined based on the number of vessels awaiting transit within each group and will be communicated through the Projected Booking Slots Availability table, published daily. Slot allocation Similarly to what was temporarily implemented on December 15, 2023, this method aims to provide additional opportunities for different customers, only one booking slot will be allowed per customer per day during the competition as shown in the following table: 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 OP, August 20, 2026 Subject: Transit Reservation (Booking) System - Rule modifications 2 Vessel category Effective date For booking period 1 Starting on booking date For booking period 1a Starting on booking date For booking period 2 Starting on booking date Regular and Super August 21, 2026 November 19, 2026 September 4, 2026 Neopanamax August 21, 2026 September 20, 2026 September 4, 2026 Under this new allocation procedure, the following rules will apply: 1. Customers that have already been awarded booking slots in previous periods, including Long Term Slot Allocation (LoTSA) and Net Zero for the same booking date, will not be allowed to obtain a slot during current competition, unless there are no additional competitors. 2. Customers that have already been awarded booking slots for the previous booking date, including LoTSA and Net Zero, will not be allowed to obtain a slot during the following booking date competition, unless there are no additional competitors. 3. The limit per customer does not apply to slots awarded through the auction process. 4. In the Neopanamax Locks, full container vessels with maximum TEU capacity will have priority to obtain a slot during competition. For vessels with the same TEU capacity, the Customer Ranking will be used as the tiebreaker criteria. Once a slot is assigned, customers will be allowed to swap or substitute the vessel with another vessel of the same or greater TEU capacity. Any customer preference submitted during the reservation slot allocation process will also be limited to vessels with the same or greater TEU capacity. 5. Unused slots from the Special Period for Super and Regular vessels for booking dates beginning November 20, 2026, will be carried over to Period 2. 6. Unused slots from the Special Period have already transferred to Period 1 for Super and Regular vessels for booking dates beginning September 5, 2026, to November 19, 2026, will be carried over to Period 2. 7. The transit conditions changes table published in Notice to Shipping N-07 will not apply until further notice. Other announcements To manage the current situation, additional modifications will be implemented and effective immediately: 1. The availability of flexibility services (such as change date, transit in advance, substitutions, etc.) may be narrowed down for all customers. For LoTSA program customers, deferrals and advanced services may be also limited under the current circumstances. 2. The Last-Minute service will be suspended until further notice. Furthermore, forfeited vessels must obtain a new slot to reschedule their transit. Measures applicable in September 1. Effective September 1, 2026, the Canal will apply the late cancellation surcharge fee (tariff number 1050.IBC9) in addition to the applicable cancellation fee, when a booking is cancelled 7 days or less before 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 OP, August 20, 2026 Subject: Transit Reservation (Booking) System - Rule modifications 3 the required arrival time and the vessel does not arrive at Canal waters within 7 days after the original booking date. 2. Due to the reduction in number of daily transits and the modifications to slot allocation criteria, the monthly calculation and update of the Customer Ranking will be frozen. Therefore, the Customer Ranking to be published on September 1, 2026, will remain in effect and unchanged until further notice. 3. Effective September 4, 2026, In Transit Times, for booked vessels will be modified to 48 hours to all booked vessels. In case a booked vessel arrives at the first set of locks the date prior to its reserved transit date, the vessel will be deemed to have transited the Canal in compliance with the ITT if the vessel departs the last set of locks prior to 2400 hours on the date after the reserved transit date. The Canal will continue offering the Net Zero slot program under the conditions published in Notice to Shipping N-07. The weekly maximum limit for LoTSA slots, including limitations by market segment and direction, will remain unchanged. However, to maintain equitable access to slots for all customers, this limit may be adjusted in accordance with Canal capacity. While the water deficit continues in the Canal watershed, the Transit Reservation (Booking) System remains the only way to guarantee a transit date. Vessels without a reservation may therefore face indefinite delays. The Canal remains committed to closely monitoring water conditions and rainfall levels and to communicating any further adjustments in a timely manner, as circumstances allow. For inquiries regarding these measures, please contact: operationservices@pancanal.com ORIGINAL SIGNED Boris Moreno Vásquez Vice President for Operations

https://pancanal.com/wp-content/uploads/.text: ADVISORIES ARE AVAILABLE AT http://www.pancanal.com FOR ETAS OR DIRECT COMMUNICATION WITH OUR OFFICES, REFER TO NOTICE N-3-2023 Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory To Shipping No. A-27-2026 August 14, 2026 TO : All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT : Underway Transfers of Provisions and Crew Changes in Pacific Canal Waters The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) reminds customers that all activities conducted within Panama Canal waters are subject to the Regulation on Navigation in Panama Canal Waters and require prior ACP authorization. Activities not expressly authorized by the ACP that may impede, delay, obstruct, or create risk to navigation, vessel operations, or lock operations are prohibited. Effective as instructed by the ACP, delivery of provisions, spare parts, equipment, or similar supplies, as well as crew changes, shall not be conducted underway in the Pacific navigation channel, including vessels proceeding southbound after departing Miraflores Locks or Cocoli Locks toward Diablo, unless specifically authorized by the ACP for exceptional operational or emergency reasons. These activities must be completed at authorized Pacific anchorage areas or other safe locations designated by the ACP before the beginning of transit, or as otherwise directed by the Authority. Masters, agents, operators, owners, vessel representatives, and launch companies shall plan and coordinate services accordingly before the vessel is underway to transit. This measure is intended to enhance safety of navigation and operational efficiency. Recent cases involving large pallets of provisions and crew changes with multiple persons and considerable baggage have contributed to prolonged movements between Miraflores and Diablo, particularly at night or during the early morning. Such conditions may increase risk during the transfer of personnel or supplies, expose launch crews and vessels to unnecessary hazards, and affect the scheduled positioning of the first Neopanamax transits in the Pacific Channel, including those subject to clear channel restrictions. The ACP will continue to evaluate Atlantic-side operations according to local anchorage limitations, traffic conditions, and prevailing weather or sea conditions outside the breakwater. Any service in Atlantic Canal waters shall be conducted only when and where specifically authorized by the ACP. Failure to comply with ACP instructions may result in administrative sanctions and liability for any costs, damages, delays, or operational impacts resulting from unauthorized activities. For additional information, please consult the Maritime Regulations available at https://pancanal.com/en/maritime-services/maritime- regulations/. For further information or assistance, please contact us at operationservices@pancanal.com. ORIGINAL SIGNED Boris Moreno Vásquez Vice President for Operations 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023

A further adjustment will take effect on September 3, lowering the maximum draft to 47.5 feet (14.48 meters). The measure is based on current water levels and projected conditions for the upcoming weeks in Gatun Lake. It is part of Canal’s ongoing water management and operational strategy aimed at ensuring the long -term sustainability of its operations. The draft adjustment will not affect the number of daily vessel transits. Instead, it reflects water conservation and resource management measures that have been in place since December 2025 as part of preparations for the 2026 dry season. These reductions represent the fourth and fifth draft adjustments announced by the Panama Canal Authority. The measures are the result of operational planning informed by lessons learned during the 2023–2024 period, as well as hydrological analyses and historical data that support the Canal’s operational decision-making process. Canal specialists continue to closely monitor weather conditions and produce technical forecasts that enable a more accurate assessment of the potential impacts of the El Niño phenomenon. This allows the Panama Canal Authority to determine and communicate any additional operational or water management measures that may be required in the coming months.

https://pancanal.com/wp-content/uploads/.text: ADVISORIES ARE AVAILABLE AT http://www.pancanal.com FOR ETAS OR DIRECT COMMUNICATION WITH OUR OFFICES, REFER TO NOTICE N-3-2023 Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory To Shipping No. A-25-2026 August 5, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Adjustment to the Maximum Allowable Draft in the Neopanamax Locks The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) continues to implement proactive water management measures to safeguard the reliability, safety, and sustainability of Canal operations. While the rainy season has commenced across the Isthmus of Panama, current watershed conditions and the continued effects of El Niño phenomenon require additional actions to ensure the long-term sustainability of transit operations. These measures will preserve service reliability while providing customers with timely and transparent information to support their voyage and supply chain planning. The Panama Canal remains fully committed to supporting global commerce through responsible water stewardship, operational transparency, and dependable service to the maritime industry. Based on the current level of Gatun Lake and recent weather projections, the ACP will implement the following adjustment in the Neopanamax Locks Maximum Authorized Draft: Effective August 26, 2026, the maximum authorized draft for vessels transiting the Neopanamax Locks will be 14. 63 meters (4 8.0 feet) Tropical Fresh Water (TFW). Additionally, effective September 3, 2026, and until further notice , the maximum authorized draft for vessels transiting the Neopanamax Locks will be 14. 48 meters (4 7.5 feet) Tropical Fresh Water (TFW). This additional adjustment supports safe navigation and operational reliability while accounting for current water levels and projected hydrological conditions. The ACP will closely monitor weather conditions, watershed inflows, and lake levels, and will provide customers with timely updates should additional operational adjustments become necessary. The capacity of the Neopanamax and Panamax Locks remains stable, and no reduction in available transit slots is being implemented at this time. To support efficient transit planning and minimize the potential for delays, customers are encouraged to take advantage of the various booking and reservation options available through the Transit Reservation (Booking) System. Furthermore, due to weather conditions changing more rapidly than originally anticipated, the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) will make every reasonable effort to provide advance notice of any future adjustments as early as possible. However, the timing of such announcements will ultimately depend on the evolving conditions and the availability of updated information. 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 OP, Subject: Adjustment to the Maximum Allowable Draft in the Neopanamax Locks For any inquiries regarding these rules, please contact our Customer Service office at the following email address: operationservices@pancanal.com. ORIGINAL SIGNED Boris Moreno Vásquez Vice President for Operations

The maximum sustainable capacity of the Panama Canal (Panamax and Neopanamax locks) is approximately 36-38 vessels per day. * In order to perform scheduled maintenance works ** In order to perform scheduled dry chamber works *** Culvert outage 3654 (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 OP, July 10, 2026 Subject: Monthly Canal Operations Summary June 2026 Panama Canal Expansion: A Decade That Transformed the World Today, the Panama Canal commemorates the tenth anniversary of the opening of its expanded waterway, a milestone that marked a turning point in the history of Panama and global trade. Ten years have passed since June 26, 2016, when the container ship COSCO Shipping Panama officially inaugurated the new Agua Clara and Cocolí Locks, ushering in a new era for global logistics. The Canal expansion represented the largest infrastructure project since the opening of the original Canal in 1914, generating tangible benefits for Panama and the world. The expansion increased the Canal’s capacity, boosting revenues for the country and consolidating the Panama Canal as an essential platform for global trade. It has also strengthened the country’s competitiveness while creating new opportunities for economic growth, investment, and employment. During the first eight months of Fiscal Year 2026 (October 2025 through May 2026), 8,593 transits were recorded, of which 27.7% correspond to Neopanamax vessels, representing 2,385 transits. Additionally, as of May 2026, more than 31,000 transits had passed through the expanded locks since their inauguration. The expanded Canal now accounts for more than 50% of the total revenues generated by the interoceanic waterway. This performance has been made possible by the recovery of water levels in Gatun and Alhajuela lakes, allowing the Canal to maintain a safe, efficient, and reliable service for international trade. 3654 (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 OP, July 10, 2026 Subject: Monthly Canal Operations Summary June 2026 Milestones That Defined the Decade Throughout its first ten years of operation, the expanded Canal has reached significant milestones that reflect its transformation and its ability to serve new generations of vessels. On June 26, 2016, the inaugural transit of the COSCO Shipping Panama was completed, followed on June 27 by the Lycaste Peace, the first liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) vessel to transit the Canal. Shortly thereafter, on July 25, 2016, the Maran Gas Apollonia became the first liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier to transit the Canal, marking the beginning of a new operational chapter for the waterway. More recently, the expansion has continued to demonstrate its relevance to international maritime trade. On August 30, 2024, the MSC MARIE set a new transit capacity record at the Panama Canal, measuring 366 meters (1,201 feet) in length with a capacity of 17,640 TEUs, underscoring the importance of the infrastructure for high-capacity Neopanamax vessels. Additionally, on March 26 of this year, the Canal welcomed the inaugural transit of Virgin Voyages with the passage of the Brilliant Lady. Virgin Voyages’ addition to the Panama route reflects the growing interest of the cruise industry in including the Canal in its itineraries, driven by the unique experience of crossing between two oceans and by the Canal’s operational reliability. 3654 (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023 OP, July 10, 2026 Subject: Monthly Canal Operations Summary June 2026 Looking Ahead: Water and Sustainability This first decade of operations has also tested the Canal’s resilience in the face of climate-related challenges, such as those experienced in 2023 and 2024, making responsible water management a national priority. For this reason, projects such as the Rio Indio Lake are part of a long -term water strategy designed to guarantee both the Canal’s continued operation and a reliable water supply for the population. A National Achievement That Continues to Deliver Ten years later, the Canal expansion continues to generate lasting benefits. It remains the country’s largest infrastructure project since 1914 and stands as a symbol of the talent, commitment, and professionalism of the 9,000 Panamanians who make its operation possible every day. As we commemorate this milestone, we celebrate not only a remarkable engineering achievement, but also Panama’s ability to adapt, innovate, and lead global trade. Recognizing Strategic Customers As part of the anniversary commemoration, Panama Canal Administrator Dr. Ricaurte Vásquez Morales and Deputy Administrator Eng. Ilya Espino de Marotta presented commemorative plaques to five Neopanamax vessels transiting the waterway in recognition of thei r valuable contribution during the first decade of operations of the expanded Canal. This initiative highlights the close partnership between the Panama Canal and the international maritime industry, as well as the essential role these partners have played in strengthening the Canal’s position as a key hub for global trade. For more information, please visit: www.pancanal.com/ampliacion

ADVISORIES ARE AVAILABLE AT http://www.pancanal.com FOR ETAS OR DIRECT COMMUNICATION WITH OUR OFFICES, REFER TO NOTICE N-3-2021 Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory to Shipping No. A-20-2026 June 9, 2026 TO : All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT : Safe Boarding Week 2026 The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) considers proper boarding facilities to be an absolute necessity to ensure the safety of their personnel, as well as others using these facilities while in Canal waters. To promote awareness and compliance with Canal requirements by vessels in our waters, the ACP will hold its annual “Safe Boarding Week” from July 6-10, 2026. During this period, the ACP will emphasize and encourage safe boarding practices on all vessels arriving at the waterway. “Safe Boarding Week” activities will involve inspections of boarding facilities by personnel who normally board vessels, such as Canal Port Captains, Pilots, Transit Vessel Inspectors, Chemists, Emergency Response personnel, Admeasurers, Deckhands, as well as ship’s agents. Vessels at Balboa Anchorage will have their boarding facility arrangements inspected utilizing the “Safe Boarding Week 2026 Inspection Checklist”. Vessel masters will be provided with the results of the inspection and those vessels deserving special recognition for excellence will be presented with plaques following the inspection. Vessels with boarding facilities determined to be below acceptable standards must correct the deficiencies prior to transit. For inquiries or additional information, please write to Arqueadores@pancanal.com This document is cancelled automatically for record purposes on July 30, 2026.
